explanation: This tests triple integration in spherical coordinates, absent from the supplied Linear Algebra topics, so it is prerequisite. Set x=r sin(φ)cos(θ), z=r cos(φ). The bounds are −π/2≤θ≤π/2, 0≤φ≤π/2, and 0≤r≤2sin(φ)cos(θ). Multiplying by the volume element gives 3cos(φ)sin(φ). After radial integration, the integral equals 6[∫cos(θ)dθ][∫cos(φ)sin²(φ)dφ]=6·2·(1/3)=4. The origin's singularity is integrable.
